title: ClearPath Managed IT Services Collections Policy: Late Fees, Suspension and Reinstatement
content:
## 1. Due date and the monthly assessment

1.1 A ClearPath Managed IT Services invoice falls due the tier's net days, in calendar days, after its posted date.

1.2 On the first day of each calendar month, every invoice of the agreement that still has an unpaid balance and whose grace period has ended is assessed one late fee.

1.3 A late fee may be assessed on an invoice only once more than the tier's grace period in calendar days has passed since the invoice falls due. The grace period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, which is the posted date plus the tier's net days in calendar days. The clock runs from the posted date of that invoice as shown on the agreement's billing ledger.

1.4 Boundary cases (hypothetical invoice posted 2025-03-01, net 30 days, grace 5 days): the due date is 2025-03-31; on 2025-04-05 exactly 5 days have passed, so no late fee may yet be assessed; from 2025-04-06 more than 5 days have passed and it may.

## 2. Amount of a late fee

2.1 The clause "Each late fee equals the late fee per month percent of the invoice's unpaid balance on the assessment day, rounded half up to the cent, or the minimum late fee if that is greater" is **no longer in force** as a rule for every late fee. It no longer governs the late fee assessed on the first day of a month, the assessment day, and posted that same day, on an invoice that is the agreement's only invoice with any amount unpaid at the end of the day before the assessment day, its late fees included, so that every other invoice is settled in full together with any late fee it carries, no other invoice having been assessed a late fee on the day of that invoice's most recent late fee; such a fee follows the late-fee schedule.

2.2 Every other late fee stays the tier's late fee per month percent of the invoice's unpaid balance on the assessment day, rounded half up to the cent, or the tier's minimum late fee if that is greater.

2.3 The unpaid balance of an invoice on the assessment day is measured as of the end of the day before the assessment day: the charges billed on that invoice (monthly fee, proration, onboarding, labor, early termination and reinstatement entries) less the payments, service credits and credit memos applied to that invoice. Late fees are excluded from both sides: late fees are not themselves assessed late fees, and service credits are deducted from the invoice they were applied to before the unpaid balance is measured.

## 3. Courtesy waiver

On request of the authorized contact one late fee may be waived as a courtesy by a credit memo reversing that fee, provided the agreement's courtesy waivers in the preceding 365 days are fewer than 1. The waivers counted are the agreement's credit memos reversing a late fee posted in the 365 calendar days ending on the day the waiver is requested, that day included.

## 4. Suspension

4.1 Service may be suspended only once the oldest unpaid invoice is at least the tier's suspension threshold in calendar days past its due date. The days past due are counted in calendar days starting the day after the due date, which is the posted date plus the tier's net days.

4.2 Boundary cases (hypothetical due date 2025-03-31, threshold 45 days): on 2025-05-15 the invoice is 45 days past due and suspension may take effect; on 2025-05-14 it is 44 days past due and it may not.

4.3 The accounting team sends the written warning the tier's warning period before suspension. Suspension stops remote and onsite support but not monitoring or billing.

## 5. Reinstatement and termination for non-payment

5.1 Reinstatement may be recorded only after every invoice past its due date has been paid in full, as shown by the agreement's billing ledger.

5.2 The clause "The reinstatement fee of the tier's reinstatement fee is invoiced on the reinstatement date and falls due under the normal terms" is **no longer in force** in that form. Every reinstatement of an agreement suspended for non-payment is now charged under the reinstatement schedule applied to the tier's reinstatement fee; the fee is still invoiced on the reinstatement date and falls due under the normal terms.

5.3 An agreement that has stayed suspended for the tier's termination period in calendar days may be terminated for non-payment, which starts the transition-out; the past-due balance remains collectible and no early termination fee is charged on that path.
